vectors.name: raw-minimal
vectors.summary: The minimal conformant raw file: one TCP session, one participant, one record. Byte-for-byte the worked example in the specification.
vectors.spec_section: Worked example: a minimal raw file
vectors.expect: Accept. The .jsonl file is the expected projection.

vectors.name: decoded-basic
vectors.summary: A decode stage's output: decoded records citing spans in the input, plus an Undecoded block covering the tail the decoder could not parse.
vectors.spec_section: A decoded file, end to end
vectors.expect: Accept. The .jsonl file is the expected projection.

vectors.name: passthrough-transport
vectors.summary: A pass-through preserving a transport layer: byte-run records with no decoder_id, provenance carried by origin on each participant.
vectors.expect: Accept. The .jsonl file is the expected projection.

vectors.name: escape-unknown-block
vectors.summary: A block of an undefined type. A reader MUST skip it by length and carry on; a converter projects it as a hex type plus its whole content in base64.
vectors.expect: Accept. The .jsonl file is the expected projection.

vectors.name: escape-unknown-option
vectors.summary: A record carrying an unregistered option id. A reader MUST skip it by len and retain it; a converter projects it into the generic options array.
vectors.expect: Accept. The .jsonl file is the expected projection.

vectors.name: escape-unknown-enum
vectors.summary: A participant whose tcp_role holds an undefined value. tcp_role is advisory, so this is not a violation: it renders as the raw number.
vectors.expect: Accept. The .jsonl file is the expected projection.

vectors.name: escape-reserved-flag-bit
vectors.summary: A record with a reserved flags bit set. A reader MUST ignore it semantically but preserve it; a converter renders it as a hex token.
vectors.expect: Accept. The .jsonl file is the expected projection.

vectors.name: annotator-decoded
vectors.summary: A pass-through preserving a DECODED layer -- the 0.10 construct 0.9 could not express. Records keep decoder_id and carry no spans; the Undecoded block is inherited, so the grandparent source is declared too.
vectors.expect: Accept. The .jsonl file is the expected projection.

vectors.name: undecoded-skipped
vectors.summary: A decode stage that deliberately declines a region -- a byte-order mark -- and says so with reason = skipped rather than claiming a parse failure.
vectors.expect: Accept. The .jsonl file is the expected projection.

vectors.name: undecoded-reason-class
vectors.summary: A non-canonical reason, which MUST carry reason_class so a consumer can still tell whether the bytes exist upstream.
vectors.expect: Accept. The .jsonl file is the expected projection.

vectors.name: sequenced-basis
vectors.summary: A hint-less UDP session marked SEQUENCED. Because it carries no seq/ack, sequenced_basis is mandatory and states what the order rests on.
vectors.expect: Accept. The .jsonl file is the expected projection.

vectors.name: reordered-decoded
vectors.summary: A stage that reorders a participant's decoded records without decoding them. It is a decode stage -- stored order defines the offsets, so reordering changes them -- and its spans run DOWNWARD against stored order. A reader that assumes spans ascend fails here.
vectors.spec_section: Layers -- filtering and reordering a decoded stream
vectors.expect: Accept. The .jsonl file is the expected projection.

vectors.name: hintless-merge-backwards-ts
vectors.summary: A hint-less session with no seq/ack, whose timestamps run backwards ACROSS participants. Every record is concurrent, so the whole order is the merge's timestamp tie-break -- but each participant's own records keep their stored order. A reader that rejects on the inversion, or that re-sorts one participant's records, fails.
vectors.expect: Accept. The .jsonl file is the expected projection.

vectors.name: merge-timestamp-tie
vectors.summary: Two concurrent records from DIFFERENT participants bearing the SAME timestamp. Before 0.12 this was a genuine tie the format did not resolve, so two conformant readers could order the file differently. The merge now breaks it by ascending participant_id, so pid 0's record precedes pid 1's.
vectors.expect: Accept. The .jsonl file is the expected projection.

vectors.name: partially-hinted-sequenced
vectors.summary: A SEQUENCED session where ONE record carries seq_start and the rest carry no hints at all. Under 0.12's definition a single hint anywhere means the session is not hint-less, so no sequenced_basis is required -- even though most of the order rests on timestamps. This vector pins that answer.
vectors.expect: Accept. The .jsonl file is the expected projection.

vectors.name: isolate-sequenced-no-basis
vectors.summary: A hint-less session marked SEQUENCED with no sequenced_basis. Recording the basis is unconditional -- the trivially-sound cases write `trivial` rather than omitting it -- so this file is semantically invalid.
vectors.expect: MAY reject the file, or isolate the session. Note WHEN: no record carries seq_start or ack, so the session is hint-less -- but a reader cannot know that until Session End or end-of-stream, since hint-lessness is a property of the records and the Session Descriptor precedes them. A checker that raises this at the descriptor is guessing; one that never raises it has not deferred the check.

vectors.name: reject-bad-magic
vectors.summary: The File Header magic is the byte-swapped pattern 5A 49 50 46, which marks a byte-swapped file. The container is little-endian by definition.
vectors.expect: Reject the file. A reader SHOULD report that the magic looks byte-swapped, which is a more useful diagnostic than 'not a zpf'.

vectors.name: reject-unknown-major
vectors.summary: version_major is 1, which this document does not define. A reader MUST reject a major it does not implement.
vectors.expect: Reject the file.

vectors.name: reject-unknown-minor
vectors.summary: version_minor is 13 while major is 0. In the 0.x regime the pair (0, minor) is the compatibility identity, so a 0.12 reader MUST reject it.
vectors.expect: Reject the file. This is the vector that distinguishes a 0.x-aware reader from one that assumes minors are always skippable.

vectors.name: reject-length-misaligned
vectors.summary: A block length that is not a multiple of 4, which breaks the alignment invariant the whole container rests on.
vectors.expect: Reject the file.

vectors.name: reject-payload-len-overrun
vectors.summary: A record whose payload_len runs past the end of its own block.
vectors.expect: Reject the file. payload_len exceeds the bytes the block's own length makes available.

vectors.name: isolate-undeclared-session
vectors.summary: A record referencing a session_id that was never declared. Well-framed, so the byte stream is trustworthy: this is a semantic violation.
vectors.expect: MAY reject the file, or isolate the offending record or session. MUST NOT silently drop it without a diagnostic, and MUST NOT invent the missing declaration. A reader that discards only the second record and keeps the first is behaving correctly.

vectors.name: isolate-duplicate-id
vectors.summary: A source_id declared twice.
vectors.expect: MAY reject the file, or isolate. MUST NOT silently pick one.

vectors.name: isolate-coverage-gap
vectors.summary: A decode stage whose output leaves part of the input stream neither covered by a decoded record's spans nor marked Undecoded.
vectors.expect: MAY reject the file, or isolate the session. The range [10,20) of input stream (session 7, pid 0) is covered by neither a record's spans nor an Undecoded block, so the coverage guarantee fails.

vectors.name: isolate-unknown-source-kind
vectors.summary: A Source whose kind is undefined. Unlike tcp_role this is load-bearing: kind decides how a span's offsets are read, so anything referencing this Source is uninterpretable.
vectors.expect: MAY reject the file, or discard the Source together with everything referencing it. MUST NOT guess a kind. Note this is the enum case that is NOT a free extension point.

vectors.name: chain
vectors.summary: A three-file provenance chain whose digests and offsets genuinely agree: raw.zpf -> decoded.zpf -> annotated.zpf. The only fixture where the recovery walk, two-hop resolution and digest verification can be exercised.
vectors.spec_section: Layers; Coverage honesty; Annotating a decoded file
vectors.expect: Accept all three. Each .jsonl is the expected projection. Each declared digest is the real SHA-256 of the sibling file it names, so a reader can verify the chain.
